openings.claim: A removable edge-registering carrier could separate sideways restraint from seal compression, avoiding dependence on tightening the rocking left corner.
openings.delta: Use four strips as two bolted rim-clamp pairs outside the marked opening. Exposed padded bolt faces register opposite hatch edges; the two straps provide balanced separation retention. Release straps to remove the hatch completely. Keep fasteners assembled and tether released pieces with cord. Drill or cut only strips. This requires suitable rim access, stop overlap and strap reach; none is established.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: balanced strap compression alone holds by friction. Registration predicts that modestly slackening straps leaves lateral travel bounded by stop clearance, while the rival predicts increased sliding. Under the final right-side card, registration should still bound travel only if edge overlap remains. Rocking, rim-clamp migration or increased travel defeats this account; no effect is established.
openings.probe: First use ruler and supplied parts to check underside access, clamp land outside the opening, 250 mm strap routing, bolt lengths and recoverable removal. If any fails, stop without modifying hatch, rim or seal. Within ninety fabrication minutes, assemble only if feasible. Use one configuration and twelve closure/pull trials within twenty observation minutes: two diagnostic trials with modestly slack and working strap settings, then ten numbered opening cycles, applying 20 N after each closure. Put the supplied 1 mm card at the right contact for the final closure. Record marked-position displacement, clamp migration, corner lift, reopening time and visible seal tears. Reject if final displacement exceeds 1 mm, reopening exceeds thirty seconds, the pull dislodges the hatch, any new tear occurs or the open aperture is obstructed. Uncontrolled preload limits rival discrimination.
assumptions: Rim geometry permits reversible strip clamps and anchors outside the marked opening.
Supplied bolts, pads, straps and cord have adequate dimensions and capacity; these are indispensable unknowns.
Low strap tension retains the hatch while permitting a meaningful registration-versus-friction comparison.

assessment: One unproven candidate. Feasibility inspection precedes fabrication; the bounded probe supplies no deployment permission or reliable performance claim. Constraints remain mandatory, including the disturbed closure.
